newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ home affordability improves in June qtr -survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ home affordability improves in June qtr -survey.

text.p: New Zealand home mortgage affordability improved for the second consecutive quarter in June as interest rates tracked down, wages lifted slightly and house prices stabilised, Massey University said in a survey released on Monday.
It said declining interest rates had again dominated the affordability improvement.
"Interest rates moved down 5.8 percent whilst house prices rose 1.6 percent during the quarter," the university said.
"Although the median dwelling price lifted over the quarter the upward trend has slowed."
The New Zealand home affordability index for June recorded an improvement of 5.1 percent. Ten of the 11 regions surveyed recorded an improvement in affordability.
Massey said the index for June also reflected a 12 monthly affordability improvement of 6.9 percent. For the first time in three years, all regions recorded 12 monthly improvements in affordability.
"Auckland's 12 monthly improvement of 11.2 percent was also significant as the highest recorded for that region since March 1994," Massey said.
